ox.service.invoke.description:
Invoke a service action: `await ox.service.invoke({ purpose, name, input?, session?, frameId? })`. Web services require an explicit frameId, including main documents; omit frameId for non-web services. Open a page or discover fresh targets with ox.web.browser.frames({ purpose, pageId }). The Host executes on that exact document without implicit navigation, page creation, or cross-service page reuse. Names use web:<domain>:<action>, api:<service>:<action>, ios:<app>:<action>, or mcp:<server>:<action>. Use supplied standard contracts or complete contracts from ox.service.inspect without rediscovering them. Runtime approvals are authoritative; never invent approval fields or repeat denied calls.

For authenticated actions or an explicit session, the Host discovers fresh accounts on the selected document and validates the selection without switching accounts. session selects account/context, not the browser page; never fabricate it. Read skills/authentication/SKILL.md for website sign-in, account selection, and authentication recovery.

Navigate explicitly with ox.web.browser.goto({ purpose, pageId, url }) before discovering the destination frame. Pages share website data. Website conversation continuations must retain their intended account and target.

Failed calls may have effects: inspect state before retrying writes. Cross-check empty, partial, or implausible results before reporting absence. Read Evolve to build or repair missing/defective web or API actions, then invoke them; Browser is not a fulfillment fallback. MCP and iOS implementations are not editable; report concrete blockers. The Host loads the frame origin's matching service on demand and shows its conversation chip; no attachment call is needed. Frame calls preserve the existing page and enforce the executing service domain. Reinspect after navigation; never automatically replay an uncertain write.

outputSchema.description: The action's output, defined by its upfront standard contract or inspected non-standard contract.

input.description: Input matching the upfront standard contract or the non-standard contract from ox.service.inspect.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

frameId.description: Required for web services, including main documents. Live document ID from browser.newPage or browser.frames. Omit for non-web services.

domain.description: Existing service domain. Direct MCP also accepts a saved connection name or unique endpoint host.

name.description: Local display name for any service kind.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

faviconUrl.description: Public HTTPS PNG, JPEG, or ICO URL for a Local MCP connection; null restores MCP-advertised icons.

ox.service.update.description:
Update an existing service by domain: `await ox.service.update({ purpose, domain, ...fields })`. Supported fields depend on the existing service kind; unsupported fields are rejected, and omitted fields are preserved. This never creates a missing service or changes its kind. All service kinds and repository sources support name as a local display-name override, applied immediately and preserved across restarts and source refreshes. Renaming leaves service identity, action names, source manifests, connections, and authorization unchanged.

Web, API, and native services support only name through this function. For Local web/API source changes, read skills/evolve/SKILL.md. Invocations load current valid source on demand. Credentials never belong in source.

Local MCP connections additionally support endpoint, transport, and faviconUrl. MCP also accepts a connection name or unique endpoint host as domain. With no fields, reconnects and refreshes tools; a name-only update does not reconnect. Set transport to auto for detection. Set faviconUrl to a public HTTPS PNG, JPEG, or ICO URL, or null to restore server-advertised icons. Explicit icons load anonymously with up to five public HTTPS redirects; server-advertised icons remain same-site without redirects. Connection changes validate before replacing and save immediately; failure preserves the old connection. Changing endpoint keeps the domain but clears old local authorization and tool approvals. Tool contracts and implementation belong to the server and cannot be edited here. Other repositories' MCP connection settings are read-only; copy them to Local before changing connection settings.

ox.service.create.description: Save a remote MCP connection with `{ purpose, kind: "mcp", name, endpoint, transport?, faviconUrl? }`. Choose an explicit display name from the product name or user request; never derive it from the endpoint hostname or use the MCP server-reported name. faviconUrl is an optional public HTTPS PNG, JPEG, or ICO URL; anonymous loading permits up to five public HTTPS redirects. MCP saves the connection to the Local repository at `repositories/local/mcp/<domain>/service.json` without connecting or requesting login; it returns the assigned domain, derived from the endpoint host, for inspect/invoke/delete. Discover non-standard tools explicitly with inspect and invoke the server's standard authorize action if authorization is required. An existing endpoint is reused; use update to change its settings or refresh tools. MCP connections save immediately. Never put credentials in the endpoint; invoke authorize. This connects to a server, not hosts one. For web/API service authoring, read skills/evolve/SKILL.md; this function creates only MCP connections.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

faviconUrl.description: Optional public HTTPS PNG, JPEG, or ICO URL for this MCP connection.

name.description: Explicit service display name chosen from the product name or user request; do not derive it from the endpoint hostname.

endpoint.description: Public HTTPS MCP endpoint without credentials. Required for MCP; omit domain.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.validate.description: Validate a complete Local web or API service draft: `await ox.service.validate({ purpose, domain })`. Checks the manifest, action installer and matching action IDs, required files, and service size limits together. Reusable skills are independent packages verified through evolve. Returns `{ domain, valid: true }` or throws with the validation error. Does not edit, load, save, or invoke service actions. Finish related source edits before calling; individual file writes do not validate service contents.

ox.service.list.description: List the selected service sources from enabled repositories: `await ox.service.list({ purpose, kind? })`. Filter by web, api, ios, or mcp. Includes available services and invalid web/API definitions with repository, manifestPath, and validationError so they can be repaired. Listing does not load service runtimes or website pages, check access, or discover MCP tools. Absence of validationError is not proof that handlers or live actions work; validate Local drafts explicitly. Use this for inventory and repair, not as a ceiling on website access. Choose research domains from the request; build missing actions through Evolve.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.delete.description: Delete a Local web service or remove an MCP connection: `await ox.service.delete({ purpose, domain })`. The user approves deletion. Inspect the target source before deleting it and preserve unrelated work. For web services, source deletion is immediate and another repository candidate may become active. There is no built-in version history to restore deleted source. MCP removal is immediate, deletes a Local definition, detaches it from this conversation, clears local authorization and tool approvals, and does not revoke access at the server or delete a non-Local repository definition.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

ox.service.inspect.description: Inspect service actions: `await ox.service.inspect({ purpose, domain, cursor? })`. Returns service metadata, available standard action IDs, and up to ten complete non-standard action input/output contracts ordered by action ID. Pass nextCursor unchanged to continue; its absence marks the last page. Never infer that an action is absent until needed pages are read. The Host loads the current valid service source on demand and shows its conversation chip; no attachment call is needed. Exact IDs take precedence; unique web/API domain matches also accept URL variants. Use the returned canonical domain for subsequent calls. Inspection does not save a service, start login, or grant action permissions. Reuse contracts returned by inspect without inspecting again; fetch another page only when needed, or batch bounded pagination when all actions are required. Standard action contracts are supplied upfront and are not repeated here. Optional website actions are available only when listed in standardActions; incompatible same-named custom actions remain in actions with their own contracts. Capability discovery failure throws rather than returning an empty successful page. Human login, verification, and payment use ordinary preparation actions followed by ox.web.browser.showPage({ purpose, pageId }). secrets lists typed saved secrets associated with the service (owned by it or granted to it) as { key, displayName, type }, never values. To use one, pass { $secret: key } in action input: use the only associated secret by default and ask the user to pick by displayName when several match. For website sign-in, read skills/authentication/SKILL.md for method and account selection, including the manual-entry choice. Filter secrets by type: account; serviceID identifies the owning service.

purpose.description: Short (<10 words) description shown to the user as the step label.

additionalProperties.description: Complete action inputSchema and outputSchema with metadata.

standardActions.description: Available standard action IDs; their contracts are supplied upfront.

secrets.description: Typed saved secrets associated with this service: owned by it or granted to it. Metadata only.

serviceID.description: Owning service namespace; only this service can read the secret. Null for an unassigned secret.

nextCursor.description: Continuation cursor; absent after the last page.

auth.description: Observed web sign-in methods. Pass one item unchanged as login input.auth; absence means unknown, not no authentication support.

items.description: Copy one advertised auth item from inspect. Required when the service advertises auth; omit only for legacy services with unknown methods.
